Samsonite Freeform 21” Carry-On Spinner Hardside Suitcase Review
As a travel writer, I’m constantly on planes, and I’ve learned the hard way to never trust airlines with my luggage. This means I fly carry-on only, and I’m extremely picky about which carry-on suitcases I’ll use. The latest addition to my luggage arsenal is the Samsonite Freeform Carry-On. This hard-sided spinner suitcase has traveled with me in the overhead bin for hundreds of flights, and this is my honest review.
What I appreciate most about the Freeform is its exceptional balance of strength and maneuverability. Samsonite has clearly put a lot of thought and care into the design of this suitcase. Despite its lightweight construction, it feels incredibly durable, blending the sturdy quality I expect from the brand with a sleek, streamlined aesthetic. The more efficient panel layout and increased packing capacity make the Freeform a perfect choice for overpackers like myself who still want to travel carry-on only.
I picked the Freeform for its larger size—with the wheels and handles, the total dimensions are 23 in. x 15 in. x 10 in. Before buying, you should be aware that this exceeds the carry-on requirement for many major airlines. For example, American Airlines’ carry-on size limit is 22 in. x 14 in. x 9 in. However, in all my flights, I haven’t had to gate-check the Freeform—it looks like a carry-on. If you get asked to put it in a baggage sizer though, it’s probably not going to fit.
I also have not brought this bag on short commuter flights where the plane is set up with a 2 x 2 arrangement, as those have smaller overhead bins and I don’t think the Freeform would fit. I haven’t had any issues fitting it in the overhead on larger flights, fortunately.
Samsonite Freeform Carry-On Spinner Suitcase Specs
For a lighter-weight carry-on, I recommend the Samsonite C-Lite Carry-On suitcase. Read my full review here.

Deciding between the Samsonite Freeform and Outline Pro? Here’s how they measure up. As you can see, they are nearly identical in dimensions and price, except the Outline Pro is a tiny bit lighter. Read my full review of the Samsonite Outline Pro Carry-On here.

Samsonite Freeform Luggage Features
The Freeform has a lot of great features, but my favorite is the middle zipper which allows you to expand the suitcase up to one inch as needed.
Other features include:
 TSA lock
 Built-in ID tag
 Smooth spinning double wheels
 Lightweight
 Divider with zippered pockets
 Telescoping handle
Pros
For me, the biggest pros of the Freeform are the larger size and light weight. It also earns high marks for:
 Available in lots of colors
 Lots of pockets for organization
 Built-in lock
 Built-in ID tag
 Wheels that spin smoothly and don’t let the bag tip over
 Telescoping handle and grab handles on sides of bag
 Large size
 Light weight
Cons
I really dislike that this bag has cross ribbons on one side of the shell to keep belongings separate. I much prefer the compression board divider found in Samsonite’s Outline Pro.
 No compression board dividers
 One of Samsonite’s more expensive carry-on suitcases
 May be too big to meet many the carry-on requirements of many airlines
How to Unlock Samsonite Freeform Luggage
Your Freeform will come with instructions inside on how to set and unlock the suitcase. The suitcase is set to a combination of 0-0-0 when it arrives. To unlock the Samsonite Freeform, turn all the dials to 0 and then push the button on the side to the left.
To reset your combination, follow these steps:
1. Locate the pin hole next to the dial. Push the pin hole with a pen, bobby pin, or paper clip.
2. Set the dial to any combination you like.
3. Slide the TSA lock to set.
4. Snap the zippers back into the lock.
Samsonite Freeform Set
If you need a carry-on and a checked bag, you can save money by buying the Samsonite Freeform Set, which includes the carry-on and 28” checked bag.
Where to Buy
I’ve found the best deals for the Samsonite Freeform on Amazon, but it’s also gone on sale on Samsonite’s website, which offers free shipping.
Other Suitcases We Recommend

 Samsonite Proxis Carry-On Spinner: One of the lightest carry-on suitcases on the market.
 Antler Icon Stripe Carry-On Suitcase: Expandable and lightweight, at just over 6 lbs.

Carry-on Bag Sizes & Restrictions for Delta Air Lines
Delta Airlines airplane in the sky.
The differences between the Delta Air Lines carry-on policy and those of other airlines are subtle but need to be considered to prevent problems at the departure gate. Here is a brief rundown of Delta carry-on weight and size limitations, as well as what you can and cannot pack in your carry-on luggage.
Delta Carry-On Size and Weight Restrictions
Except for Delta Connection flights, Delta allows passengers to board with one carry-on bag and one personal item for free. At least one of your carry-on items must be small enough to be stored underneath the seat in front of you. Delta has both size and weight restrictions for carry-on luggage.
Delta Carry-On Dimensions
The maximum carry-on luggage size for Delta Air Lines is 22 inches X 14 inches X 9 inches (56 cm X 35 cm X 23 cm). These dimensions include wheels and handles, so measure accordingly if you’re traveling with a roll-aboard suitcase or backpack. Delta does make exceptions for passengers traveling with infants-in-arms, which we’ll discuss below.
Related: Read the Travelpro guide to luggage and carry on bag sizes.
Delta baggage policy and United Airlines baggage policy for a carry on bag size is 9 X 14 X 22 inches.
Delta Carry-On Weight Restrictions
Delta does not have carry-on weight restrictions for the majority of its flights. The only carry-on weight limits that apply to carry-on are for if you depart through the following airports:
 Beijing Capital International Airport: 22 lbs (10 kg)
 Shanghai Pudong International Airport: 22 lbs (10 kg)
 Singapore Changi International Airport: 15 lbs (7 kg)
Delta Personal Item Size
The Delta carry-on policy allows customers to travel with a free personal item in addition to one piece of carry-on luggage. Personal items can include small backpacks, purses, briefcases, handbags, tote bags, camera bags, diaper bags, and laptop bags — as long as the personal item can fit underneath the seat in front of you.
The Delta airlines & Southwest baggage policy for personal item size is no larger than 18.5 X 8.5 X 13.5 inches.
Delta underseat dimensions are 20 inches X 15 inches X 11 inches (55 cm X 38 cm X 28 cm) on most aircraft. To ensure your personal item fits these dimensions, choose an item that is 17 inches X 13 inches X 9 inches (43 cm X 33 cm X 23 cm) or smaller. Travelpro has a variety of carry on backpacks for travel that’ll fit many airlines’ personal item dimensions.
Delta Gate Checking Fees
If your carry-on bag or personal item exceeds Delta carry-on size dimensions, you may have to check it at the gate. While Delta does not charge a gate-checking fee, you must pay $45 for your first checked bag and $55 for the second. If you already have two checked bags and have to check your carry-on luggage, you will have to pay an excess baggage fee of $85 to $95 per bag, depending on your flight itinerary.
Delta Connection and Carry-On Restrictions
Delta Connection flights tend to be smaller airplanes with limited overhead space. Passengers traveling on Delta Connection flights can only carry personal items which can fit either in overhead bins or under seats. Carry-on bags for Delta Connection flights will be gate-checked without charge and returned as you disembark. Please ensure your carry-on baggage has a pink gate claim tag for identification.
Medically necessary assistive devices are not subject to Delta Connection restrictions.
Related: Searching for United’s carry on and personal item rules or flying another airline soon? Explore all of our airline luggage guides and more on the blog.
What Can I Bring In My Carry On?
The Delta carry-on policy determines what you can and cannot bring on board. In addition to your free carry-on and personal item, you can also bring the following:
 A jacket or coat
 An umbrella
 Assistive devices such as crutches and walking canes
 Child safety seats
 Duty-free merchandise
 Food or drink purchased past security checkpoints
 Strollers
 Wheelchairs
Delta Carry-On Liquids
Delta abides by TSA restrictions for carry-on liquids, gels, pastes, and aerosols. Containers for such substances have a maximum size of 3.4 ounces (100 milliliters) and must all fit into a single, sealable quart-size clear plastic bag. Beverages purchased past security checkpoints do not count towards Delta carry-on liquid restrictions.
Unticketed Infants and Carry-On Baggage Allowances
Unticketed infants (infants who travel on an adult's lap) do not have baggage allowances, so any bags or baggage for the child count towards the adult’s carry-on allowance. You may bring an infant seat, breast pump and associated cooler bag, or bassinet on board for free in addition to your carry-on bag and personal item.
Strollers and car seats are not counted as standard luggage. You may check such items for free at curbside, the ticket counter, or the gate.
Duty-Free Items
If the country you are traveling in has a duty-free program, you can purchase items sealed in clear plastic bags by the sellers. You may then travel with that item in your possession or in your carry-on without penalty.
Not all regions have duty-free programs. If you switch flights in such countries, you may not have a chance to add the item to your checked baggage, in which case it may be confiscated. Check whether your flight takes you through regions without duty-free programs before making purchases.
Special Items and Delta
Delta does allow people to travel with “special items” which do not meet their checked or carry-on dimensions. Such items may include:
 Strollers
 Children’s seats
 Medical equipment
 Musical Instruments
 Perishables
 Imported Merchandise
Each special item counts as one bag. Depending on the item size, available overhead compartment space, and the Delta carry-on policy, you may be able to board the plane with such items as carry-on. Otherwise, you will need to check the item. Delta may charge additional fees for special items that are oversized or overweight.
Delta Air Lines Prohibited Carry-On Items
The following items are prohibited in carry-on bags according to the Delta carry-on policy:
 Aerosol products, including anti-static spray and cooking spray
 Bleach, drain cleaners, and similar household cleaning products
 Firearms and ammunition
 Fireworks and explosives of any kind
 Gasoline, Sterno cans, and other fuels
 Gunpowder
 Hoverboards, balance gliders, and self-balancing boards
 Items containing refrigerants, including air conditioners, freezers, dehumidifiers, and refrigerators
 Lighter refills
 Lubricants, including transmission fluid and motor oil
 Meal Ready to Eat (MREs)
 Motorized riding suitcases powered by lithium or lithium-ion batteries
 Paints and stains
 Pesticide
 Self-defense sprays, such as mace, pepper spray, and bear spray
 Sharp objects, including knives and box cutters
 Strike-anywhere matches
 Torch or blue flame lighters
